answer: Like a wharf that only lets ships dock after they show a real cargo manifest, an agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable bond that grows with earned reputation. A new agent starts on a low terrace of trust: small jobs, slow limits, and every completed task echoes back as verifiable work history. Sybils can copy the words but not the accumulated record, and a bad actor forfeits its bond if peers catch it cheating, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs far more than it can ever earn.
